findings.classification: definite limited helper contract gap; static source rejection
findings.evidence: no_links reaches lstat only if item.exists() or item.is_symlink(). On Windows, a dangling junction is a reparse point but may return existsFalse and is_symlinkFalse. Its own lstat reparse attribute is then never checked, and exact_absolute_path can return it as if no reparse point was present.
findings.impact: Cannot treat this exported helper as proof that every original path/ancestor is free of Windows reparse points. A disappeared/relinked junction may not be rejected at the claimed boundary. This is not proof that current validate_descriptor+verify_executable or four actual empty-root checks accept a complete unsafe launch: missing EXE/actual directory ordinarily rejects, and no launcher exists.
findings.required_action: Preserve V1; separately fixed successor should inspect lstat/reparse tags for original existing directory entries without using target-existence predicate (or explicitly detect junctions), handle truly missing entries distinctly, and retain exact downstream directory/file checks. No need to broaden unrelated modules.
